name: Kami-Shakujii
tagline: Shinjuku in 34 minutes and Shibuya in 43 minutes. Served by 1 line. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥70,000 to ¥80,000.
summary: The station is in Nerima City, where Seibu run 1 line between them. Journey times to the main business districts are 43 minutes to Otemachi, 34 minutes to Shinjuku, 43 minutes to Shibuya and 64 minutes to Shinagawa. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥70,000 to ¥80,000. The station stands 50.6 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 2.6 m. The land around the station is close to level.

terrain.note: The station sits on the higher side of the ground around it, at 50.6 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 49.7 m to 52.3 m, a difference of 2.6 m.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls outside the projected inundation area. Even so, 1 of the nine points within 400 m fall inside the area, and the deepest projection there is 0.5 to 3 m. On the whole, the flood projection here is among the smallest in the 23 wards.

medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 2 clinics and 4 pharmacies. The nearest hospital is 医療法人社団 杏順会 越川病院, about 17 minutes' walk from the station. The next nearest is 千秋会田中脳神経外科病院, about 18 minutes' walk. "Hospital" here means a facility OpenStreetMap records as one. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 1 line serve the station: Seibu Shinjuku Line.
congestion: Seibu Shinjuku Line runs at 148% of capacity in the morning peak. The busiest stretch is 下落合→高田馬場, which this station is not on. At 100%, the ministry's scale describes every passenger either seated or able to hold a strap or pillar. The figures describe each line's busiest stretch, so the stretch you ride may be easier.

rentRange.note: Around this station, One room ¥70,000 to ¥80,000 and 1K ¥80,000 to ¥90,000. 1LDK ¥120,000 to ¥130,000 and 2LDK ¥150,000 to ¥160,000. These are the per-station averages published by LIFULL HOME'S, Yahoo! Real Estate and at home, averaged together and rounded down to the nearest ¥10,000 (our own survey). All three are asking rents, so what tenants finally agree can be lower. Within the same station area the figure moves a great deal with the age of the building, the walk from the station, and whether the flat faces a main road.

rentReason: A one-room flat here goes for ¥70,000 to ¥80,000. Set against how long it takes to reach the central business districts, that is on the high side. a small projected flood depth and schools and parks within walking distance pushes the figure up. On the other side, only one line, the {line}, serving the station holds it down. For 1LDK, though, the sources differ by ¥30,000 or more. They count different sets of properties, so read those figures as a range rather than a point.

neighbours.lead: Kami-Igusa is ahead on how close the centre is, and little else separates the two.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Kami-Shakujii. It is served by the same lines as Kami-Shakujii. To Toranomon, for instance, Kami-Igusa is 3 minutes quicker. Rents, flood projections and the rest differ little.

neighbours.lead: For the number of medical facilities, Musashi-Seki; for how close the centre is, Kami-Shakujii.
neighbours.note: About 1.5 km from Kami-Shakujii in a straight line. It is served by the same lines as Kami-Shakujii. To Toranomon, for instance, Musashi-Seki takes 3 minutes longer. On the number of medical facilities, Musashi-Seki comes out ahead.

leads.terrain: The ground around the station is almost level, so you can choose where to live without thinking about slopes.
leads.groceries: There are 8 supermarkets within walking distance, and the nearest is 1 minutes on foot.
leads.hazards: The station itself is outside the projected flood area, but blocks nearby are inside it.
leads.stationNote: Only the Seibu Shinjuku Line serves this station, so when it stops you walk to another station.
leads.rentRange: Set against how long the commute takes, rents here are on the high side.
leads.medical: The number of clinics and pharmacies within walking distance is about average for the 23 wards.
leads.congestion: Morning loading on the lines here is about average for the 23 wards' stations.
leads.noiseSources: The big roads are far enough that traffic noise is unlikely to bother you.
